segment.description: Greasy Creek (GNIS 01328320) in Polk County — the Ocoee-drainage creek near Coker Creek/Archville that the catalog describes ('TWRA spring-stocked... small and flashy'). Identity locked to the Polk County / HUC-8 06020003 (Ocoee) namesake: the historic USGS gauge 03563100 'GREASY CREEK NEAR ARCHVILLE, TN.' (18.5 sq mi drainage, 35.1179, -84.5705) and TDEC station TDECWPC-GREAS000.4PO (35.1220, -84.5569) both fall on this creek. This is NOT the Warren County Greasy Creek (Collins River drainage) that a flattened 2026 TWRA schedule table visually paired with a Collins River row, nor the Bradley County Greasy Creek (HUC 06020002) that appears in the Chickamauga-side station lists.
segment.boundaries: Full named creek: Ocoee River confluence near Archville/Caney Creek (~35.1093, -84.5719 per NHD flowline) upstream through the Coker Creek area, Polk County, HUC 06020003. No sub-reach boundaries documented by an agency.

coldSource.notes: Small, flashy Ocoee-drainage creek (18.5 sq mi at the historic Archville gauge) in the Cherokee NF / Coker Creek area; no dam and no spring-influence documentation found. No published reach elevation located on an agency page.

holdover.detail: No holdover evidence found: no creel data, holdover notes, or multiple independent angler reports were located for the Polk County Greasy Creek.

wildPopulation.detail: No creek-specific wild-trout documentation found: the creek carries no entry on TWRA's trout-regulations lists (wild trout waters / special regulation / delayed harvest) and no agency fish-community inventory was located. Trout presence rests entirely on the seasonal stocking program.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: The historic USGS gauge at Archville (03563100) never exceeded 19.5 degC in its 1970-1972 summer grabs — cool enough for trout survival year-round in principle — but the record is a discontinued 10-sample 1970s series with no modern temperature or biological confirmation.
